facts.fact: NIDA Director General Josephine Mukesha says NIDA's electronic system records civil-status events including births and deaths, and the same agency runs the electronic identity card enrolment.
NIDA says its electronic system records nine categories of civil-status information including births, with births registered at health facilities since 2020 and at Cell offices otherwise.
NIDA says its electronic system can record deaths among nine categories of civil-status information.
NIDA reports birth registration at approximately 96 per cent, up from 70 to 80 per cent, without tying the rate to the digital system.

RWA.note: Gives 8.3 million verified and 7.2 million biometrics captured, but no population share.

facts.fact: RADIOTV10 reports the new electronic identity card will be available from birth, each person receiving a unique number kept for life, while the existing card is issued from age 16.

RWA.note: No operator, maintenance or ownership stated.
No register keyed on the ID number stated.

facts.fact: NIDA says nationwide biometric enrolment for the new electronic identification system began in 2025, with 7.2 million people's facial images, fingerprints and iris scans captured.

RWA.note: Registration at places of birth is stated but not that the entry is made digitally at the office or how many offices.
